subject: RFP: model entitlement matrix & pin-backstop technical pack
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@nebula-ai.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@nebula-ai.com
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: RFP ITEM: model entitlement matrix, provenance evidence, and pin-backstop requirements

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick intro call today. As part of Nebula's evaluation pack we need a technical pack that covers three focused areas for every model in Redwood's public catalog that we might use: (1) license entitlements and redistribution constraints, (2) verifiable provenance (source artifacts, commit hashes, SBOM-like metadata), and (3) your recommended pinning / update policy including emergency rollback (what we're calling a "pin-backstop").

Can you provide a single deliverable that maps each model (name + version) to: license text snippet, source origin (URL + commit or release tag), proof-of-origin artifact (PDF or signature), the exact pinning identifier you recommend, and the operational steps for both planned updates and emergency re-pinning? Nebula will include this in the RFP scoring (security & legal).

We're specifically evaluating how Redwood handles: upstream license changes, provenance gaps for community checkpoints, automated notification windows for customers, and practical rollback guarantees when a new model release has a regressive behavior. If you can attach an exemplar for one model we discussed (atlas-7b-open), that would be ideal.

Timing: can we get the pack within 3 business days? If not, propose a timeline and any gaps we should be aware of.

Thanks — look forward to the pack.

Emily Tran
Senior Product Procurement Manager
Nebula Analytics
procurement@nebula-ai.com

Attachments: none

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@nebula-ai.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP ITEM: model entitlement matrix, provenance evidence, and pin-backstop requirements

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask and the scoring criteria. We'll assemble a technical pack that follows the exact mapping you outlined. High-level plan:

- Deliverable: single ZIP (spreadsheet + PDF artifacts + markdown playbook) that maps models to license clauses, origin URLs + commit hashes, proof-of-origin artifacts (signed manifests), recommended pin identifiers, and standard operating procedures for planned updates and emergency pin-backstops.
- Owners: Karthik will lead the provenance extraction and proof artifacts; Monica will validate license snippets and legal constraints; I'll own the pinning/playbook and the package delivery.
- ETA: target 48 hours (by 2026-11-19T12:00:00Z). If we hit provenance gaps for community-sourced checkpoints we'll call them out explicitly in the matrix.

I've attached a short exemplar and a draft matrix (internal): model-entitlement-matrix.xlsx; proof-of-origin-chain.pdf; pinning-playbook.md. Will exchange the ZIP via the Drive link and provide a one-hour walkthrough if you'd like.

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: model-entitlement-matrix.xlsx (stub), proof-of-origin-chain.pdf (stub), pinning-playbook.md (stub)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Tran <emily.tran@nebula-ai.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T18:20:00Z
Subject: Draft: entitlements, provenance artifacts & pinning policy (atlas-7b-open exemplar)

Team / Emily —

Attaching the draft excerpts we plan to include in the technical pack. Below is the concise, machine-readable summary we will put into the spreadsheet (we include explanatory notes after each row):

1) model: atlas-7b-open | license: Apache-2.0 (with attribution appendix) | origin: https://model-repo.example/atlas/atlas-7b-open tag v1.2.3 | provenance proof: signed_manifest_sha256: 3f7a...c1e (see proof-of-origin-chain.pdf, p.3) | recommended pin: atlas-7b-open@v1.2.3 (immutable)
   - Notes: Apache-2.0 permits commercial use; we surface attribution text and any downstream redistribution constraints in a license_snippet column.

2) pinning policy (summary):
   - Immutable pins: customers can pin to exact artifact identifier (model@sha or model@vX.Y.Z).
   - Floating pins with semantic stability: we support model@major (e.g., atlas-7b@7) which advances only on major releases after quality gates pass.
   - Canary updates: default rollout: 5% traffic canary for 24-72 hours with evaluation metrics (latency, perplexity delta on holdout prompts, safety classifier flags).
   - Pin-backstop (emergency rollback): automated circuit breaker when safety regression > threshold or hallucination spike is detected; system re-pins affected customer traffic to last known-good pin within target RTO 15 minutes (configurable in Dedicated/Private plans).

3) provenance evidence approach:
   - For curated upstreams: we store upstream release URL, git tag/commit, and an automated SBOM-like manifest (weights checksums, tokenizer version, compile flags). Manifests are timestamped and signed by Redwood's build account.
   - For community checkpoints without complete upstream metadata: we issue an internal attestation that enumerates observed artifacts and open gaps (e.g., missing upstream commit). Those rows are flagged in the matrix with a 'provenance_gap' column and remediation recommendations (e.g., escrow copy, additional testing).

4) license-change handling:
   - We run an automated license monitor (weekly) for known upstreams and notify customers via 14-day and 30-day bulletin windows for permissive-to-restrict changes.
   - If license becomes incompatible with existing customer entitlements, we support export/escape strategies (e.g., freeze on last permitted pin, migration guidance to an alternative compatible model).

5) audit & logs:
   - Every pin change (manual or automated) is recorded in audit logs (immutable append-only) with pre/post metrics and PGP-signed action tokens. Logs are retained per contract (default 13 months).

Attachments included in the pack: model-entitlement-matrix.xlsx (draft rows), proof-of-origin-chain.pdf (signed manifests excerpt), atlas-7b-proof-snippet.txt (commit/hash snippet), pinning-playbook.md (operational runbook).

I'll push the ZIP to the Drive link and will follow up with the final XLSX that includes a column-level glossary for your legal team.

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Model Ops
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@nebula-ai.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T10:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft: entitlements, provenance artifacts & pinning policy (atlas-7b-open exemplar)

Thanks — the draft is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we finalize scoring:

1) For atlas-7b-open you reference signed_manifest_sha256: is that a Redwood signature only, or is it a signature chain that includes upstream author verification? For procurement/legal we prefer a chain that includes upstream attestation where available.

2) If an upstream license changes retroactively (e.g., permissive -> restrictive), you say you provide a "freeze on last permitted pin" — can you confirm whether that freeze is enforceable for customers on Hosted plans, and what the process is for customers to request a copy of the last permitted artifact?

3) On provenance gaps: does Redwood have a remediation SLA — e.g., within X business days we will obtain escrow/archive or perform an independent re-build to create a new signed manifest?

We need the above confirmed and the exemplar proof attached so our legal/compliance can verify. Can you do this by EOD today? We have an internal scoring meeting tomorrow morning.

-Emily

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@nebula-ai.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft: entitlements, provenance artifacts & pinning policy (atlas-7b-open exemplar)

Emily —

Short answers inline: 1) Signature chain: where upstream author signatures exist we include them verbatim in the signed manifest and anchor them in our timestamped signature. If upstream signature is absent we generate a Redwood-signed attestation that records observed source artifacts and hash chain (we label that attestation clearly in the pack). See proof-of-origin-chain.pdf (p.2 shows the chain example for atlas-7b-open).

2) Freeze on hosted plans: yes — for Hosted customers we maintain immutable artifact caches for any pin a customer has requested. If a license changes in a way that would retroactively restrict usage, we will maintain the last permitted pin for that customer and provide programmatic export access per contract (API + one-time secure download). Customers on Dedicated/Private have additional export and escrow options by default. Process: submit a support/escrow request (we include a Doc ID in the pack) and we deliver a signed artifact with access tokens; access is audited.

3) Remediation SLA for provenance gaps: standard remediation target is 10 business days for curated gap resolution (e.g., obtain upstream artifact or escrow copy). For high-risk or contract-blocking gaps we have an expedited track (3 business days) and can provide an interim mitigant (extended canary, extra safety gating) while we obtain definitive evidence.

We uploaded the ZIP to the shared Drive link and attached the small atlas proof snippet (atlas-7b-proof-snippet.txt). If you'd like, Karthik and I can join a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the artifact chain and the pin-backstop behavior under SLO conditions.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
